title: Time Jump — 12:00 PM PDT: Third Wave Larger, Warning Still in Effect

fields.narration: It is now 12:00 Pacific Daylight Time, Tuesday 13 April 2027. It has been 1 hour 46 minutes since the earthquake and 8 minutes since the M 7.6 aftershock. The National Tsunami Warning Center's Tsunami Warning for the Oregon coast is still in effect. Tsunami Message Number 4 was issued at 11:45 PDT. At 11:58 the Port Alder tide gauge recorded a third wave at plus 4.1 meters above predicted tide. That is higher than the 3.6 meters at 11:06 and the 2.4 meters at 10:38. Each wave so far has been bigger than the one before. Cold rain is still falling, and it is 49 degrees. About 3,800 visitors and residents are packed onto Spruce Hill with no shelter, no toilets and no water. Eleven hospital patients are still on the Kellerton Station 3 apron under the cracked canopy. Cedar Court residents are spread out between the assembly area and the roadside. The 911 backup positions here at the EOC have 54 calls holding. Highway 101 at the Alder River bridge and Highway 6 on the Neskin grade are both cut, and no outside help has reached the county. On the hill and on the phones, people are pushing harder every minute to be allowed to go back down. EXERCISE EXERCISE EXERCISE.
worldState: Clock: 12:00 PDT, Tuesday 13 April 2027. EOC on generator; commercial power out countywide.
NTWC Tsunami Warning for the Oregon coast remains in effect: current product is Tsunami Message Number 4, issued 11:45 PDT. It has not been cancelled.
Port Alder tide gauge (observed): 10:38 +2.4 m; 11:06 +3.6 m; 11:58 +4.1 m above predicted tide. The gauge is reporting; oscillation continues.
M 7.6 aftershock at 11:52 PDT, about 60 km WNW of Port Alder: USGS automatic solution, not yet reviewed. Strong aftershocks remain possible.
Spruce Hill: about 3,800 people in cold rain (49°F) with no shelter, toilets or drinking water.
Kellerton Station 3 apron: 11 hospital patients still under the canopy that cracked in the aftershock.
Cedar Court residents are split between the assembly area and the roadside; not all are accounted for in one place.
911 backup positions at the Kellerton EOC: 54 calls holding.
Highway 101 Alder River bridge (south abutment dropped, gas main leaking) and Highway 6 Neskin grade (landslide near milepost 9) are both closed. No outside resources have reached the county.
Front Street, harbor and campground sirens are still silent; MarlowAlert text and voice delivery remain degraded.
Public pressure to return to the waterfront is growing; no return order has been given.
fields.facilitatorNote: Check that every status board (WebEOC Tsunami Status in particular) now shows Message Number 4 and the 11:58 +4.1 m reading. Listen for Command to state plainly that the XL/XXL evacuation stays in place, and for someone to name the return criteria: NTWC cancellation, then gauge below 0.3 m for two hours, confirmed by the Warning Coordinator, Sheriff and Harbor Master. If the room starts talking about a partial or phased return, ask who has confirmed those conditions.
fields.scenarioTitle: The Second Wave — Cascadia Rupture, Tsunami Evacuation & Message Discipline

instructorNote: This card opens Phase 3. It shows players that each wave has been larger than the last, so they have to hold the evacuation while conditions on the hill get worse. Watch whether Command confirms that the XL/XXL evacuation stays in effect and that the return criteria have not been met, and whether all roles update to Message Number 4 and the 11:58 gauge reading.
